title: Boundary phenomena for slow recurrences:finite and infinite critical sets
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05424v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For $T_m=\{(m-1,m),(m^2-1,m^2)\}$, the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on $\Theta_m(\log x)$ integers up to $x$ whenever $m\ge3$, whereas for $m=2$ its complete set of slowest integers is $\{1,2,25\}$. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.

title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.

title: Construction, Enumeration and Duality of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets of Order $2pq$
authors: Paul Lascabettes, Sidney Ali, Alexandre Popoff, Moreno Andreatta
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05441v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order $2pq$. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order $2pq$, and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order $6p$. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order $2pq$ can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary $2p$-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order $2pq$ and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.

title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
authors: Albert Joon Lee, Woosik Kim, David E. Bernal Neira
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.

title: On Parallel Sums of Set-Valued Operators: Monotonicity, Paramonotonicity, and Decomposition Invariance
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05523v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate structural properties of the parallel sum of set-valued operators in a real Hilbert space, with particular emphasis on monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, and paramonotonicity. We examine the decomposition-invariance property of the parallel sum of two paramonotone operators and provide a direct proof based on monotonicity and the equality of admissible decompositions. This approach establishes the required orthogonality relations without invoking the Attouch--Th{\'e}ra Duality duality framework. We also revisit the classical maximal-monotonicity property of the parallel sum and present an alternative graph-based derivation involving an auxiliary shifted operator. Furthermore, we study the parallel sum of a set-valued operator and the normal cone operator associated with a closed linear subspace. Explicit characterizations of its values, domain, and range are presented, and a decomposition-independent representation is obtained under paramonotonicity through the orthogonality of the underlying subspaces. These results provide a unified and self-contained treatment of selected properties of parallel sums and clarify the role of paramonotonicity in their structural behavior.

title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order H\"older Smoothness and Uniform Convexity
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05527v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order H"older-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose $p^{th}$-order derivatives are H"older continuous with degree $
u$ and parameter $H$, and that are uniformly convex with degree $q$ and parameter $\sigma$. When these orders match, namely, $q = p + 
u$, we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order $p$ requires $\Omega\left(\left( rac{H}{\sigma}ight)^{ rac{2}{3(p+
u)-2}}\log rac{\Delta_0}{\epsilon}ight)$ oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of $\Delta_0$ to $\epsilon$. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global H"older smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.

title: A First Closed-Form Robin Parameter for Optimized Schwarz Waveform Relaxation as a Function of Iteration Count, Overlap, and Time Window Length
authors: Alejandro Alfonso Rodriguez, Martin J. Gander, Felix Kwok
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05576v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Schwarz waveform relaxation (SWR) is a parallel-in-time iterative method for the solution of evolution problems and belongs to the class of Parallel-in-Time algorithms that have received increasing attention over the past three decades. For parabolic problems, SWR converges linearly over long time intervals and exhibits superlinear convergence on short time intervals. Since the introduction of optimized variants (OSWR) nearly three decades ago, determining the optimized Robin parameter when OSWR is applied on bounded time windows has remained an open problem.
  We introduce here a new analytical approach that, for the first time, yields a closed-form expression for the optimal Robin parameter in the transmission conditions for the one-dimensional heat equation with two overlapping subdomains. The resulting formula explicitly characterizes the dependence of the optimal parameter on the iteration number, the overlap size, and the length of the time window. Beyond resolving this long-standing optimization problem, our analysis provides a framework that can be extended to more general settings, including higher-dimensional problems, multiple subdomains, and higher-order transmission conditions.

title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05607v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational $\alpha$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $n\alpha$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.

title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation
authors: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05626v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth $d$ with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension $k$, is the narrowest, and let $K$ be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in $[\delta, 1 - \delta]$ are uniformly recovered from $m \gtrsim k(d \log(K/k) + \log(1+\log(1/\delta)))$ measurements.

title: Calder\'{o}n's complex interpolations of variable-exponent Fofana spaces
authors: Nouffou Diarra, Pokou Nagacy, Sekou Coulibaly
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fofana spaces, introduced in the framework of Wiener amalgam spaces, can be viewed as generalizations of Morrey spaces. These spaces have attracted considerable attention in recent years and have found applications in the study of partial differential equations. In this paper, we investigate their variable-exponent counterparts. More specifically, we describe Calder\'{o}n's, first and second, complex interpolations of Fofana spaces with variable exponent, as well as the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals. Our results recover, as special cases, those already known for (classical) Fofana and Morrey spaces.

title: Comparative analysis of numerical methods for X-ray 3D reconstruction from sparse views
authors: Melitine N. Bardi, Konstantinos K. Delibasis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05645v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular structures from a limited number of X-ray projections is a severely underdetermined and ill-conditioned inverse problem. This work presents a unified matrix-free computational framework for evaluating iterative numerical methods for sparse-view cone-beam tomography. Forward and backprojection are implemented from ray-voxel intersection lengths computed with the Amanatides-Woo traversal algorithm, avoiding explicit construction of the large sparse system matrix. We systematically compare ART, SART, SIRT, gradient descent (GD), and Krylov subspace methods, including Conjugate Gradient, LSQR, and GMRES. The common matrix-free operators and geometry are used for all methods, allowing consistent comparisons under matched conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on gradient scaling using scalar step sizes, Jacobi preconditioning, and diagonal Hessian majorization, together with L1, Tikhonov, and total variation regularization. Numerical experiments use five three-dimensional coronary vessel models reconstructed from ten simulated X-ray projections under noise and scattering conditions, and are extended to real X-ray projections of a static thin-vessel phantom. Performance is evaluated in terms of convergence, computational cost, volumetric overlap, contrast-to-noise ratio, vessel diameter and centerline errors, and projection consistency at an unseen viewing angle. The results show that total-variation-regularized gradient descent with diagonal majorization provides the best overall reconstruction performance within the investigated computational budgets. By contrast, the tested Krylov implementations achieve limited geometric recovery despite higher computational cost. These findings emphasize the importance of appropriate gradient scaling and regularization for stable and computationally efficient sparse-view tomographic reconstruction.

title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05649v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(G)\leq (1-\delta)d$, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $$\gamma(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}{\delta}$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges. For real Banach lattices the bound is $O(qC/\delta)$. The proof estimates where a random walk first leaves each coordinate level set. As a consequence of the bound, if $n$-vertex graphs in a fixed-degree expander family embed with bounded distortion into spaces with bounded $C,K$, then $q$ must grow at least as fast as $\log n$. This order is attained in $\ell_q^n$.

title: The Galois actions on braided fusion categories
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05677v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This note harmonizes two classical topics: minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories and the Galois action on modular fusion categories. Their common generalizations are Galois-modular extensions, which always exist when a braided fusion category $\mathcal{B}$ is pseudounitary. Each extension induces a Galois action on the simple objects of $\mathcal{B}$. Up to integral equivalence, the Galois-modular extensions of $\mathcal{B}$ form a torsor over an explicit group of homomorphisms from $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ to the invertible objects of order dividing two in the symmetric center $\mathcal{E}$ of $\mathcal{B}$. If $\mathcal{E}$ is Tannakian and $\mathcal{B}$ has a minimal modular extension, all minimal modular extensions induce one canonical Galois action. We prove that many facts about the modular data of modular fusion categories extend to pseudounitary premodular fusion categories as well via the Galois action.

title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05696v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

title: Discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for higher order finite element de Rham complexes
authors: Johnny Guzm\'an, Pratyush Potu, K. Olav Tyssvang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincar\'e operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.

title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations for the Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
authors: Gabriel P. Braun, Marcia Fampa, Nelson Maculan, Renan V. Pinto
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Given a set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an integer $k\ge0$, the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most $k$ Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-$M$ constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, with up to $50$ terminals and $9$ Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.

title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05736v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
authors: Andr\'e Tits, Pierre-Antoine Absil, No\'e Tits
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05772v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A<K$ users is active in the delivery phase. We recently showed that (i) under uncoded placement, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, so that coded placement is needed; and (ii) for $AM\leq N$, every classical scheme with row-wise placement, including the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV), can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code, which removes the penalty. In this note, we show that every point of the scheme of Yu, Maddah-Ali and Avestimehr (YMA) for a classical system with $A$ users is achievable in the hotplug model for every $K\geq A$. Each user is associated with a hyperplane and each file with a homogeneous polynomial; each user caches the restriction of the polynomial to its hyperplane, and the subfiles seen by the active users are the values of the polynomial at the points where their hyperplanes meet. This is a projective Reed-Muller code, which reduces to the Reed-Solomon code when each subfile is cached by one user. We then show, by an existence argument, that every classical scheme whose cache is a linear compression of the Maddah-Ali-Niesen cache and whose correctness holds for generic coefficients can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field; this includes the interference elimination (IE) schemes of Tian and Chen. These embeddings complement the Reed-Solomon one, which allows any row-wise placement and any delivery. Together with past work, our results show that every point attained by a GV, YMA or IE scheme ($N\leq A$ for IE), and every corner point of the linear tradeoff for $A=N=3$, is achievable in the hotplug model with a load that does not depend on $K$. Whether the optimal hotplug tradeoff depends only on $A$ remains open, but these results support a positive answer.

title: Near-Optimal Complexity of Finding Approximate Local Minima of Nonconvex Finite Sums
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05807v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the component-oracle complexity of finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite sums under mean-squared averaged smoothness with parameter $L$ and a $\rho$-Lipschitz average Hessian. Each query returns the value, gradient, and one Hessian-vector product of a component. We show that the complexity in the high-accuracy regime $\varepsilon\le c_0L^2/(n\rho)$ is $\tilde\Theta(n^{3/4}L^{1/2}\rho^{1/4}\Delta\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ for a sufficiently large initial gap $\Delta$. We attain the upper bound by adapting the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to averaged smoothness. Our lower bound assigns the bridge edges of a nested chain to random components; a replicated spectral construction gives the same bound for unrestricted randomized algorithms. Under individual smoothness, a factor of $n^{1/4}$ remains for $\varepsilon\le cL^2/(n^2\rho)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the complementary low-accuracy regime, we propose PathVR, which uses $\tilde O(n+\sqrt{n}L\Delta\varepsilon^{-2})$ queries and matches a lower bound from dense weak hiding.

title: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05831v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a Bayesian information-theoretic framework for proving functional inequalities for log-concave measures. Motivated by Klartag and Ordentlich, we establish a unified equivalence between $\Phi$-Sobolev inequalities and Bayesian estimation lower bounds: for a large class of smooth convex $\Phi$, a log-concave measure $\mu$ satisfies a $\Phi$-Sobolev inequality with constant $C>0$ if and only if for $X\sim\mu$, any $t>0$, and any real-valued measurable $f$, the Bayes risk of estimating $f(X)$ under the $\Phi$-Bregman loss from the Gaussian additive observation $Y_t=\sqrt tX+G, G\sim N(0,I_n)$ is at least a $1/(1+Ct)$-fraction of that of the trivial estimator.
  Combining it with direct information-theoretic arguments, such as testing-to-estimation reductions, we obtain old and new functional inequalities:
  - For the Poincar\'e inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=(x-1)^2$, we give a simple static information-theoretic proof that the Poincar\'e constant of an isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $O(n^{1/2})$, first proven via stochastic localization in the seminal work of Lee and Vempala.
  - For the log-Sobolev inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=x\log x$, we prove that all smooth $K$-subgaussian log-concave measures $\mu$ satisfy $C_{\mathrm{LS}}(\mu)\lesssim K^2n^{1/4}$, surpassing the recent state-of-the-art bound of $O(K^2n^{1/2})$ by Bizeul. In parallel and independent work, OpenAI claimed the optimal bound $O(K^2)$ in their October 6, 2026 release of 722 papers.
  - Finally, we give a Bayesian reformulation of the common structure of the three recent proofs of the Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits conjecture, a dimension-free Poincar\'e bound for isotropic log-concave measures [BK26; BKL26; SZ26]. Tools from the study of the "low-degree MMSE" in computational complexity of statistical inference motivate and recast key steps and quantities of these proofs.

title: Learning Coarse Spaces for Two-Grid Methods from Smoothed Errors with Applications to High-Contrast Porous Media Flow
authors: Chenglong Bao, Chen Cui, Ruohua Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05837v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient two-grid solvers for high-contrast parametric elliptic problems require coarse spaces that capture error components poorly reduced by local smoothing. As these components vary with the problem parameters, repeatedly constructing parameter-adaptive coarse spaces can be computationally expensive. We propose a coarse-space learning method based on finite-step errors generated by additive Schwarz smoothing. For each training parameter, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of smoothed-error snapshots in the discrete energy inner product defines a reference coarse space. A continuous-coordinate neural generator is then trained using a basis-invariant, whitened subspace loss, enabling the prediction of parameter-adaptive coarse spaces on unseen grids. We establish discrete perturbation estimates relating coarse-space discrepancies to the associated nonsymmetric two-grid operators and derive conditional finite-step Krylov residual-polynomial bounds without assuming stationary energy contraction. Numerical experiments on high-contrast interface problems, moving-interface Darcy flow, and nonlinear Forchheimer flow demonstrate effective solver performance across varying parameters and grid resolutions. On the finest static test grid, with approximately 264 times as many degrees of freedom as the training grid, the learned spaces achieve FGMRES iteration counts close to those of parameter-specific POD references and comparable to GenEO spaces, while substantially reducing repeated coarse-space construction costs.

title: The Invocation Bottleneck in LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed and What Must Be Traded
authors: Zhe Yan, Yihao Liu, Antonio Boffa, Huanchen Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05871v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) compress text far better than classical compressors, but LLM-based compressors are slow, particularly during decompression. We argue that their decoding time has two fundamentally different sources. Execution redundancy, such as per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, and token-by-token encoding, is work that the coded output does not require and can be removed without changing a single output bit. Sequential dependency, one model call per decoded token, is inherent to lossless decoding and cannot be removed by better execution, only traded for more calls or for more bits. We remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline whose block-parallel encoding is made lossless in half precision by batch-invariant kernels, speeding up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing its compression rate. We then study the two ways of trading sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC), characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix, and identify the workloads in which fewer model calls are worth that cost.

title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05879v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

title: Weak and strong convergence of a general splitting approach for monotone multioperator inclusions
authors: Minh N. Dao, Matthew K. Tam, Thang D. Truong
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05884v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study a general forward-backward splitting approach for monotone inclusion problems that simultaneously accommodate set-valued, monotone Lipschitz continuous, and cocoercive operators. Weak convergence is established under a general setting. Strong convergence is obtained when both the maximally monotone operators are linear relations and the monotone Lipschitz continuous and cocoercive operators are linear. When the set-valued operators are normal cones to closed linear subspaces, we derive an explicit characterization of limit points of generated sequences using a new technique. Numerical experiments on a quadratic minimization problem with multiple-set split feasibility constraints are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

title: Dimensionally absolutely stable but non-diagonalizable $T$-meshes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05923v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct an infinite family of rectangular \(T\)-meshes whose conformality-vector-space dimension is constant over all structurally similar geometric realizations, although the meshes are not diagonalizable. For every integer \(d\ge 2\), the construction has \(2(d+2)\) \(\Tl\)-edges and intersection graph \(K_{d+2,d+2}\). Every \(\Tl\)-edge contains at least \(d+2\) vertices, so no edge is vanishable under the usual vertex-count criterion for bidegree \((d,d)\) and smoothness \((d-1,d-1)\). We prove that the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class. Its generator is the outer product of two vectors of barycentric interpolation weights, extended by four zero coordinates. Non-diagonalizability follows by examining the last edge in any proposed diagonalizing ordering. Thus, for the geometric structural similarity class specified here, diagonalizability is not a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability.

title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $\zeta_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1

<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.

title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
authors: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<q><\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.

title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the Lebesgue measure of wandering continua and related invariant sets in Julia sets, using the hyperbolic area method recently developed by Ye. For entire functions of finite type, we show that a wandering continuum of positive area must escape to infinity uniformly. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we show that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.

title: Magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields: a Fourier-finite difference approach
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems for two-dimensional magnetic Schr\"odinger operators with nonuniform periodic magnetic fields and periodic scalar potentials, and develop a hybrid Fourier-finite difference discretization. A Landau-type gauge is constructed by solving a periodic Poisson equation. Under the integer magnetic flux condition, the magnetic Bloch boundary conditions are incorporated through shifts of Fourier-mode indices. The method combines link-variable-based covariant central differences in the $x$-direction with a Fourier pseudospectral discretization in the $y$-direction, yielding a Hermitian discrete Hamiltonian. The resulting eigenvalue problems are solved using a LOBPCG method. Under appropriate regularity assumptions, we establish a fully discrete consistency residual estimate of order $O(h_1^2+N_2^{-s})$. With suitable spectral separation and eigenspace dimension-preserving conditions, error estimates of the same order are derived for isolated eigenvalues and their associated eigenspaces. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence in the finite difference direction and rapid error reduction with increasing Fourier resolution, and illustrate band degeneracies and eigenstate distributions in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields.

title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction
authors: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yixin Ying, Liu Cao, Vanlin Sathya, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Channel sounding in Wi-Fi multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems must balance channel state information (CSI) accuracy against CSI acquisition overhead. Device mobility causes channel aging, while autoregressive CSI prediction introduces errors that accumulate over sounding intervals. However, standardized statistical channel models cannot fully capture the environment-specific channel dynamics encountered in physical artificial intelligence (AI) applications, motivating the use of Sionna-based ray tracing to evaluate CSI prediction under device mobility and evolving propagation geometry. This paper develops a dynamic sounding framework that integrates autoregressive CSI prediction with signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-constrained interval selection. A Transformer with rotary position embedding that converts device positions into CSI sequences predicts CSI across multiple subcarriers for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges. We formulate sounding-interval selection as a predicted average-throughput maximization problem under per-stream SINR lower-bound constraints, including CSI acquisition and processing overhead. A prediction-error perturbation analysis provides the SINR bounds, and cumulative-sum enumeration globally solves the finite single-variable problem. Actual SINR feasibility holds whenever the prediction errors satisfy the bounds. Ray-tracing experiments assess channel prediction, trajectory transfer, and autoregressive prediction errors. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% over stale CSI for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories, respectively.

title: Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model
abstract:
arXiv:2611.05977v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by $24.6\%$--$86.6\%$ in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.

title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geometric multigrid methods for conforming finite element discretisations classically require a nested mesh hierarchy, forcing coarse meshes to be conforming, which is unsuitable for general domains. In order to eliminate this geometric constraint, we introduce and analyse a family of multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners. At the first level, a conforming Lagrangian discretisation on a fine simplicial mesh is preconditioned by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation posed on an arbitrarily agglomerated coarse mesh. At the subsequent levels, the coarse problem is solved by a geometric multigrid method for that polytopal discretisation on further agglomerated meshes, so that the whole hierarchy is generated from the fine mesh by agglomeration alone. We consider two polytopal discretisations, a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and a hybrid high-order method. The prolongation operator at the first level is an element-wise interpolation onto the fine mesh followed by nodal averaging, preceded in the hybrid high-order case by a local potential reconstruction. For point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers, we prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $O((H/h)^3)$, where $H/h$ is the coarsening ratio, and by $O((H/h)^2)$ for the DG variant with penalty proportional to $H/h$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on structured and unstructured meshes with agglomerates generated by automatic clustering algorithms, confirm the robustness of the preconditioners.

title: Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06031v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case. We also introduce a vertex bialgebra analogue of quantized universal enveloping algebras and construct explicit quantizations to all orders of Cartan type Lie conformal bialgebra structures on $\operatorname{Cur}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These results contribute to the first author's broader programme of developing shifted symplectic chiralization as a geometric method for constructing chiral analogues of Poisson-Lie structures via $n$-shifted symplectic geometry, and exploring its connections with AKSZ theory and quantization.

title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06059v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.

title: Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06080v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.

title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
authors: Siyu Cen, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhi Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06112v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.

title: The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertia Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06125v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, in which every objective is the sum of a smooth convex term and a proper closed convex extended-valued term, and the proximal subproblem retains a separate offset for each objective. The momentum coefficient may depend on the computed trajectory. For a two-parameter root momentum rule we prove boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. The analysis is organized as a chain of basic estimates, an energy identity, coefficient asymptotics, and auxiliary lemmas that are reused in every regime. For the critical parameter $\alpha=3$ we establish the finite bound $u_0(x^N)\le 2\ell R/[N(N+3)]$, square summability of the displacements, displacement decay $O(1/N)$, and convergence of the full sequence to a weak Pareto point. The remaining little-o question at $\alpha=3$ is shown to be exactly the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy, so it is separated from the large-$O$ estimate rather than left as a missing step. For $1<\alpha<3$ we give the rate $O(N^{-(\alpha-1)})$ and for every $\alpha>0$ the qualitative conclusion $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A table summarizes the rate picture over the whole positive range of $\alpha$, and a JOS1 experiment illustrates the predicted little-$o$ separation.

title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06153v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,\alpha}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.

title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $\epsilon^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
authors: Haijun Gao, Xi Li, Xiaoli Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $\epsilon$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $\epsilon$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $\epsilon^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $\epsilon$. In particular, by introducing $H^{-1}$ approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.

title: Fano's Inequality and Channel Capacity in the Individual-Sequence Regime
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06182v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive an individual-sequence analogue of Fano's inequality, replacing entropy by Lempel--Ziv (LZ) complexity and probability of error by empirical error frequency. In the setting considered, an arbitrary encoder maps a message to a channel input sequence $\{x_t\}$, the channel maps the input to an output $\{y_t\}$ in a completely arbitrary manner, and a block finite-state decoder produces an estimate of the channel input from the output. The individual-sequence Fano inequality lower-bounds the empirical symbol-error frequency in terms of the LZ complexity of the channel input conditioned on the channel output. This leads to a channel coding converse: reliable communication at a given rate is possible only if that rate does not exceed the individual-sequence LZ channel capacity, defined as the LZ mutual information maximized over channel inputs and minimized (worst-case) over a noise set. We also prove a matching achievability theorem for the class of \emph{symbol-wise invertible} channels, in which the channel output at each time $t$ is $y_t = f(x_t, v_t)$, $v_t$ being a `noise' variable, and $f(\cdot,v)$ is a bijection for every fixed $v$. This class includes group-additive channels $y_t = x_t \oplus v_t$ studied by Feder and coworkers. For such a channel, any rate below the LZ capacity is achievable with vanishing per-message error frequency, simultaneously for every $v^n$ in a given noise set $\mathcal{N}$, provided $\mathcal{N}$ is closed under block permutations; this condition is satisfied by any noise set that depends on $v^n$ only via its type class with respect to such blocks. The achievability uses a universal decoder that requires no knowledge of the channel and no feedback.

title: Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
authors: Ante Sikirica, Ivana Lu\v{c}in, Marta Alvir, Tin Matulja
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06183v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.

title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
authors: Chi-Kwong Li, Ming-Cheng Tsai, Ya-Shu Wang, Ngai-Ching Wong
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+\gamma b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|\gamma|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.

title: $C_2$-Cofiniteness of Permutation Orbifolds I: Relative $C_1$ Descent
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06201v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a relative $C_1$-cofiniteness criterion for $C_2$-cofiniteness of finite group orbifolds. For permutation actions on a simple, self contragredient, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type, it suffices to check a single relation for a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra. This reduces the problem to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree. An exact calculation then proves cofiniteness for a family of nonsolvable permutation orbifolds without restricting the central charge.

title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels
authors: Xu Pei, Bin Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Yi Zhang, Haiyan Fan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06205v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.

title: Accessibility of collapsed Anosov flow
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.

title: Equilibrium webs and stability for arbitrary families of endomorphisms of projective spaces
authors: Fabrizio Bianchi, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06211v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Br\'evard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.

title: Quasi-norms on $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization and Approximation by Conic Splines
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06212v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We first show that a regularizer on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form $g=q^\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$, where $q$ is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such $q$ the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate $h^2\asymp n^{-2/(d-1)}$, in the $L_\infty$-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the $L_1$-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an $\ell_1$-norm of second differences as regularity index.

title: Calmness Modulus of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas via Second-Order Admissibility
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06224v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We resolve the open problem of deriving an exact, closed-form algebraic formula for the calmness modulus of $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex constrained feasible set mappings $\mathcal{F}(b) := \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \colon f_t(x) \le b_t, \, \forall t \in T \}$ under right-hand side perturbations at a given pair of the graph $(\bar{b}, \bar{x})$.
  First, under the condition $0_n \in \mathrm{int}\left(\mathrm{conv}\left\{ \nabla f_t(\bar{x}) ,\; t \in T(\bar{x}) \right\}\right)$, we prove that the calmness modulus coincides with the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential.
  Second, for general $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex systems where the previously mentioned interior condition does not hold, we introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over the active indexes. We show that this filtered family, $\mathcal{D}^0_2(\bar{x})$, yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying solely on nominal data.

title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06233v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.
